title: A typo'd id reads as a successful completion
description:
tinytodo/store.py line 17 defines `complete(self, item_id)`. Lines 18-20 read `item = self._items.get(item_id)` / `if item is None:` / `return None` — so completing an id that was never added returns None and looks, to every caller that does not check, exactly like success. Support have twice closed a ticket that was never marked done.

Make it raise instead. Define `UnknownItem` in tinytodo/store.py, subclassing KeyError, and raise `UnknownItem(item_id)` from `complete()` when the id is not in the store — so `str(exc)` contains the id that was asked for. Completing a known id must behave exactly as it does now: it sets `done` to True and returns the item dict. Every test already in tests/test_store.py must still pass unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: tinytodo/store.py defines UnknownItem and it subclasses KeyError
complete() raises UnknownItem for an id that is not in the store
str() of the raised exception contains the id that was asked for
complete() on a known id still sets done to True and returns the item
every test in tests/test_store.py still passes, unchanged
